articles.headline: Bethel Church Parsonage
articles.author: Progress [VERIFY pseudonym]
articles.summary: For the Christian Recorder. The members of Bethel have taken up collections for a parsonage; the writer asks whether it would not be best to build the parsonage on the ground adjacent to the church. This ground belongs to the Corporation though leased upon ground rent to other parties. The lot running 72 feet east from the north-east corner of 6th and Lombard St. has not paid the church one cent of ground rent for eight or ten years. The church surroundings are a disgrace: old frame shanties; on the corner of 6th and Lombard the tavern is never closed; in the yard of the shanty next to the church a swing kept for hire, used on the Sabbath by lads who annoy the Sabbath-school. Urges the Corporation to repossess the ground and erect a handsome parsonage.

articles.headline: Our Appointment (editor appointed to Bethel; wishes to go South)
articles.author: James Lynch
articles.summary: At the recent session of the Philadelphia Conference, we were appointed to the pastoral charge of Bethel Church of this city, in connection with the editorial control of the Christian Recorder. Notwithstanding the great amount of labor this double appointment would involve, we would attempt it with willingness and hope, did not our whole heart say, 'Go South!' ... on the eve of his leaving for Georgia we asked [Bishop Wayman] if there would be impropriety in tendering our resignation ... and he answered in the negative. We have not heard from him yet.

articles.headline: Valedictory (James Lynch resigns the editorship)
articles.author: James Lynch
articles.summary: To the Readers of the Christian Recorder.--It is with deep regret I announce my peremptory resignation of the Editorial control of the organ of the A. M. E. Church. ... For a little over sixteen months I have held the position. ... Between myself and the General Book Steward, who was formerly the editor, though he has steadily maintained the illegality of my appointment, which displaced him, there is the best of feeling ... They impel me to go to a Southern State, and unite my destiny with that of my people ... I hope that God will bless my colleague, Rev. Elisha Weaver, and that as the Travelling Agent, Rev. Theodore Gould, can perform most of the labor which devolved on Brother Weaver, I have no doubt that my avowed course will not prove prejudicial to the interests of the Book Concern. Stand by the Recorder. Friendly readers--Farewell! James Lynch, Editor of Christian Recorder.
people: General Book Steward, formerly the editor (Rev.)

articles.headline: Valedictory First, Valedictory Last (Elisha Weaver resumes the editorship)

articles.summary: Readers of the Christian Recorder.--You have already learned of the resignation and the appointment by the Bishops, of Rev. articles.summary: Harriet Sipple Henrys was a bright child about four years old, at the time I became acquainted with her. She was a scholar in Bethel Sabbath School, Philadelphia, and a member of Mrs. Martha Collins' class. The mother of Harriet being stewardess on an ocean steamer, left her in the care of a personal friend by the name of Henrys ... At the memorable revival of religion in Bethel Church, under the pastoral care of the venerable John Cornish, assisted by Elder, now Bishop Campbell, Harriet gave her heart to God ... She was married to ... a young man by the name of Jones ... On her last voyage to California she contracted a heavy cold ... consumption.

articles.headline: To the Ohio Conference (Book Concern debt: ten dollars per preacher; Philadelphia Conference's $7,000 call)
articles.summary: Dear Brethren. Will you not be so kind as to carry out without delay your resolution in regard to the Book Concern, that each brother, on going to his station or circuit, was to raise not less than ten dollars and forward it to us by the first of July 1867. We would say to all of our brethren throughout the connection, holding a charge, that the Philadelphia Conference passed resolutions to call upon our different Conference districts to ask our brethren to go to work and raise seven thousand dollars, so as to have our property paid for before the meeting of the next General Conference ... The Committee of the Book Concern will expect this amount to be raised by the last of September or the first of October. We expect Philadelphia district to take the lead in this matter.

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Church and the M. W. Grand Lodge A. Y. M. of Pennsylvania -- exchange of presentations
events.location: Philadelphia (Bethel A.M.E. Church and the Grand Lodge)
events.description: Quite recently the M. W. Grand Lodge A. Y. M. for the State of Pennsylvania presented to Bethel A.M.E. Church a handsome silver Communion Service. On Tuesday, March 26th, the Trustees and Stewards of Bethel Church made a return presentation to the Grand Lodge, consisting of a handsome Bible, Gavel, and silver Square and Compass, with a written declaration of Christian friendship, enclosed in a beautifully carved walnut frame, bearing the signature of the Pastor, Rev. events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Church, fifty-first session -- opening, committees and trials (first installment)
events.description: Editorial note: the Conference commenced its session last Saturday (May 18); Bishops Quinn and Wayman present; also Rev. John M. Brown, Corresponding Secretary of the P. H. and F. Missionary Society, and Rev. James A. Shorter, agent for Wilberforce University. Visitors: Rev. R. F. Wayman (Baltimore Conference), Rev. W. H. Winder (New York Conference), Rev. J. W. Devine [printed Devina, VERIFY] (Ohio Conference), Rev. A. L. Stanford recently from Savannah. Report headed PHILADELPHIA A. M. E. CONFERENCE, FIFTY-FIRST SESSION: the Conference met at Bethel Church, Sixth Street, Philadelphia, May 18, 1867, Bishop Wayman presiding, Bishop Quinn of Indiana present and assisting. Religious services by Rev. Jacob Mitchell. James Lynch elected Secretary, H. J. Rhodes assistant. On motion of Jonathan Hamilton the standing committees were appointed: Public Worship: J. Hollen, R. P. Gibbs, G. E. Boyer, W. M. Watson, T. Gould. Finance: Theodore Gould, J. Hollen, R. P. Gibbs, G. E. Boyer, W. M. Watson. Missions: D. P. Seaton [printed Leaton/Seaton, VERIFY], Stephen Smith, W. Stevenson. Education: James Lynch, J. C. Cornish, P. Gardner. Memorials: B. Lynch, D. Draper, Jos. A. Nelson. Temperance: G. Hamilton, J. P. B. Eddy, W. H. Chase. Book Concern: H. J. Rhodes, J. H. Smith, J. Mitchell, B. Lynch, J. P. B. Eddy. Sunday Schools: N. H. Turpin, G. T. Waters, W. R. Norris. Wilberforce: Elisha Weaver, W. H. Williams, J. H. Henson [VERIFY]. Conference Stewards: Peter Gardner, Jeremiah Young, N. H. Turpin, Theodore Gould. To publish the minutes: James Lynch. Hours 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. (on motion of E. Weaver). Jacob Jay appointed Marshal. The Bishop noted no member had died during the year. Financial reports from circuits and stations showed prosperity; the best was that of Burlington, N.J., by Jacob Mitchell. Characters examined: A. C. Crippen charged with unkind treatment of his wife; William Moore represented the church; charge sustained; a motion to locate him was opposed by Stephen Smith and lost; on motion of James Lynch, A. C. Crippen was suspended from all official functions for one year. H. J. Rhodes complained of by William Moore for maladministration: not sustained. Thomas M. Kinnard complained of by E. Weaver for neglect of duty (he had opened a doctor's shop and followed dentistry to support his family): exonerated. Thomas V. Pierce complained of Jacob Jay for entering a civil suit against him; on motion of Jonathan Hamilton the Bishop appointed a committee. (To be continued; appointments not yet printed in this issue.)

events.description: 'For the Christian Recorder.' Second day: religious services by Rev. G. T. Waters; General Book Steward Rev. Pierce, a regularly ordained elder of the British Methodist Episcopal Church, be admitted; William Moore spoke for him; admitted. D. P. Seaton offered Frisby J. Cooper of Wilmington, Delaware, for local membership (admitted), and presented Isaac Parker, an ordained minister of the African Union Church. Benediction by Rev. B. Lynch. Third day: Bishop Wayman presiding; services by Rev. W. H. Williams; Stephen Smith moved that local preachers not attending by Wednesday 10 o'clock be fined $1; on motion of W. H. Williams money was appropriated to give Father Bulaugh (editorial prints Boulaugh), the oldest minister in the connection, immediate relief. Rev. Isaac Parker took the A.M.E. ordination vows and on motion of Stephen Smith was admitted. Jacob Mitchell offered Jacob Jay (laid over). T. A. Cuff of Reading offered Walter Thomson for the itinerancy and Samuel Underhill for local membership. Edward Lawe offered Joel Fisher for local membership (not admitted). H. J. Rhodes of West Philadelphia offered W. D. Johnson and George Washington. James Hollen offered Littleton Dennis and Benjamin Lloyd for local membership, then withdrew the applications to make corrections. William Williams of Lancaster offered Robert Boston; William H. Chase of Montrose offered Jacob Wilkeholm for the itinerancy; Isaiah S. Taylor of Delaware offered Peter Loper; R. P. Gibbs offered Ephraim Wilson, a local deacon from Zion A.M.E. Church (parchments approved, admitted). Rev. Dr. Taylor, corresponding secretary of the American Bible Society, and Mr. Jewell were introduced; Rev. John M. Brown responded; E. Nelson, charged by the Trustees of Germantown with fraud, found him guilty; James Lynch moved reconsideration, opposed by E. Weaver and H. J. Rhodes, lost; Lynch gave notice of a new trial. Committee on Temperance (chairman W. H. Chase) urged temperance societies in all charges. On motion of E. Weaver no church meetings Wednesday evening; all invited to the Book Concern mass meeting at Bethel Church. Benediction by Rev. Mr. Alston. Fourth day: Bishop Wayman presiding; services by Rev. George Thornton; on James Lynch's resolution a new investigation was granted Rev. Joseph Nelson, committee Jeremiah Young, J. V. Pierce, W. H. Williams, W. W. Grimes and T. A. Cuff. events.name: Book Concern mass meeting during the Philadelphia Annual Conference
events.description: Great mass meetings were held during the sitting of the Philadelphia Annual Conference. The one in behalf of the A.M.E. Book Concern was an immense gathering; Bethel Church was literally packed. Revs. James A. Shorter, Brown, Woodlin, Weaver, Lynch, and Messrs. Isaiah Wears and A. Fields spoke; a collection was lifted. The missionary meeting was likewise large: Rev. John M. Brown, the corresponding secretary, spoke; about $75.00 raised; $25 paid by friends to make Bishop A. W. Wayman a life member of the society.

Crummill, 'the founder of our league', an earnest worker for the liberation and enfranchisement of his race; copy to the family and to the Christian Recorder. By order of the President, William B. Purvis; Solicitor, James Tillman. Dated Bensalem E. R. L., May 23d, 1867 (printed 1887).

events.name: Concert of the Excelsior Base Ball Club

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference, fifth to ninth days (synopsis)
events.description: The new committee on Joseph A. Nelson's case (charged with fraud by the trustees of Germantown) found him perfectly innocent; money raised was paid out for repairs, mortgage, travelling expenses, salary and legal fees. Peter Loper, Walter Thompson and Jacob Wilsheim (printed 'Wilshelm'; earlier 'Wilkehelm') admitted to the itinerancy on trial; Littleton Dennis, Frisby J. Cooper, Samuel Underhill, Robert Boston and Benjamin Lloyd admitted to local conference membership on trial. Ephraim Wilson, a local deacon from Zion Church, admitted. W. H. Turner, H. H. Lewis and Benjamin Darks admitted into full connection. Committees on Book Concern, Education, Temperance and Sabbath-schools reported; a plan to relieve the Book Concern of its financial embarrassment. Jacob Jay, by vote of Conference, reprimanded severely by the Bishop. Conference pledged $500 for the Missionary Cause and a share of Bishop Payne's tour to England. Ordination of deacons. Vineland Circuit divided. Conference Stewards reported. Resolutions passed recommending the congregation of Wesley Church, Hurst street, to sell their building and move to the western part of the city. Report on Wilberforce University. $200 loaned by the Missionary Fund to the Book Concern at 6 per cent for one year. $125 paid to Rev. John M. Brown, Corresponding Secretary of the Parent Home and Foreign Missionary Society. Standing Committees and appointments announced (as published last week). The Annual Sermon preached by Rev. Peter Gardiner. Minutes delayed: 'We have had the Recorder to edit, Bethel Church to attend to, and the minutes to prepare.'

events.name: Trustees of the A.M.E. Book Concern -- accept Lynch's resignation; Weaver to fill the editorial chair
events.description: The Trustees of the A. M. E. Book Concern met, Philadelphia, June 13th, 1867. Present: Revs. Elisha Weaver, James Lynch, Stephen Smith, William Moore, N. H. Turpin, H. J. Rhodes (by proxy). Jacob Mitchell was not in the State. The resignation of Rev. James Lynch was considered; regret expressed, but he would not yield. The resignation was accepted and resolutions passed (his course highly honorable; thanks and prayers), signed Stephen Smith, William Moore, H. J. Rhodes, N. H. Turpin, Elisha Weaver, Chairman. Lynch responded with deep emotion. On motion of N. H. Turpin, it was resolved that Rev. Elisha Weaver fill the editorial chair. E. Weaver, Chairman of Book Committee.

events.name: Funeral procession of Brother Henry Williams (?), Mount Holly, N.J. (Sons of Temperance and Masonic lodge)
events.location: A.M.E. Church and cemetery, Mount Holly, N.J.
events.description: Reported by T. Gould, Agent, A.M.E. Book Concern (Theodore Gould, the travelling agent). On 'last Sabbath' (computed as Sunday June 23, 1867; the letter is undated, so the date is inferred) the funeral of Brother Henry [VERIFY] Williams, who died the morning of the 12th inst. in his 47th year. He was a local preacher, class leader, trustee, sexton and Sabbath School superintendent of the A.M.E. Church, a Past Grand Master in the Masonic Order and a life member of the Grand Lodge; 'the Burlington Lodge turned out as citizens'. The Sons of Temperance turned out five divisions (four colored, one white), met in their hall, formed into line and marched to the house of the deceased, where bearers were detailed. Procession order to the church: the ministers, the corpse, the friends, the Sons of Temperance, the Masonic Lodge, and the citizens. Church filled, as many outside in the yard. Rev. James Frisby [VERIFY] preached from Rev. 14:13, citing an acquaintance of nearly twenty years. Procession then to the cemetery. He was born in the South, left as a lad 'for the sake of freedom', did not see his mother for 25 years until after the war, then brought her to his home; survived by wife and aged mother. Gould then returned to Burlington, where Brother Jackson, the local preacher, preached and Gould closed; he got subscribers and a donation 'to be acknowledged hereafter'. PARADES/PROCESSIONS topic (funeral procession, mixed-race temperance divisions); MIGRATION (self-emancipated Southerner reunited with mother).
attendees: Agent, A.M.E. Book Concern; preached at Mount Holly and Burlington (Rev.)

events.name: Elisha Weaver's visit to the New England and New York A.M.E. Conferences (New Haven; New York; Weeksville L.I.)
events.location: New Haven, Conn.; New York and Brooklyn; Weeksville, L.I.
events.description: From Weaver's 'Our Visit to the New England and New York Conferences' (ext_C has the article and the appointments; this event adds the itinerary and names read from crops). Weaver arrived in New Haven on the night of the 16th inst. (printed '16th'; ext_C's summary has '15th') at 8 1/2(?) P.M.; Bishop Quinn and the members were at Rev. E. T. Williams' house at a strawberry feast. Sabbath sermon for the ordination of several brethren by Rev. J. W. Hurley(?). Monday the Conference finished business, held a demonstration on behalf of the Book Concern, a missionary meeting at night, and the Bishop read the appointments; at a quarter to 11 a number of brethren left for the New York Conference on the steamer Continental, among them Revs. H. J. Rhodes, J. M. Brown, Turpin and others. Thanks to the 'Daughters of Conference' of New Haven, New Bedford, Newport, Providence, Boston and Bridgeport. New York Conference: arrived Tuesday morning, Bishop Wayman presiding. Visited the anniversary of the Old Folks' Home of New York (about two thousand present). Visited the African Civilization Society in Weeksville, L.I., with Rev. Theo. Gould: received by Rev. R. L. Perry, editor of the People's Journal; five or six ladies setting type; the eldest son of Mr. Thomas Hamilton in the paper business; Rev. Mr. Wilson, business agent. Met Prof. W. H. Day, editor of the Zion Standard and Weekly Review. New York appointments read 'last Monday': Rev. H. Dorrell [VERIFY] to Bethel Church, Philadelphia; Rev. J. M. Williams to Trenton, N.J.; Rev. N. H. Turpin to Bridge St., Brooklyn. MIGRATIONS/clergy movement; only Philadelphia Conference clergy and bishops linked; New York and New England names are text only.
attendees: visitor, General Book Steward and editor (Rev.)
